tasks.short: Examine income-property income records and operating costs

steps.what: Read income records, leases and operating costs and verify comparison inputs
Repeat specified period totals, cost ratios and lease-income comparisons
Examine exceptions and determine sustainable income and relevant operating costs

tasks.design: Test native comparison tables in the appraisal application in {OTHER}. Repeat explicit totals and ratios from checked records, while the appraiser reads leases, resolves classifications and assesses sustainable property income.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated arithmetic accompanies substantive examination of income and expenses.
tasks.enabler_now: Native tables can reuse specified periods, categories and comparison rules.
tasks.still_hard: Separating recurring income and normal costs from unusual or unsupported items.
tasks.human_edge: Judge what the records imply for this property's valuation.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated arithmetic with unchanged income assessment responsibility.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: appraisal calculation tables can repeat specified totals and ratios, while interpreting leases and sustainable income requires professional judgement.

assumptions: Provisional boundary is examining income records, not a separately commissioned report. OTHER is the appraisal calculation application. No new review log or send is created.

Property owners supply records, but the appraiser reads and verifies property ID, lease dates, period, amount, currency, cost category and supporting source in s1. Extraction, category decisions and missing-record follow-up are not free normalized inputs.

Native tables are tested first. Only 25 repeated manual arithmetic/comparison points are removed, not existing runtime. s3 retains full interpretation, independent checks and unsupported-case repair; excess correction lowers the estimate.
Any ordinary working-note save stays fully retained and ungated.
unknowns: Record format and actual arithmetic share
research_questions: Replay examination of one income property and count extraction separately from repeated arithmetic.

incremental.description: Maintain period and category comparison rules

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Remove 25 arithmetic points less 1.5 upkeep. Mixed cash/accrual records and irregular lease periods require manual reconciliation; repeat only 6 points of compatible period totals: 6 minus 1.5 = 4.5.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Inspect building scope and verify quantities, condition and replacement specifications
Select appropriate valuation-manual rates and assess professional cost-estimator advice
Calculate quantities times selected rates and explicit location or date adjustments
Check coverage, omissions and calculation results and determine the replacement-cost estimate

tasks.design: Configure native quantity-rate calculations in the building valuation application in {OTHER}. Retain inspection, rate selection and appraisal of cost-estimator advice, then independently check the complete replacement-cost estimate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated multiplication and adjustment calculations accompany scope and rate judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Native estimate tables can calculate explicit selected quantities, rates and adjustments.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising omitted work and choosing rates for nonstandard buildings.
tasks.human_edge: Define credible replacement scope and judge whether the estimate covers it.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated estimate arithmetic with unchanged cost-estimate responsibility.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: building-cost applications calculate quantity-rate estimates and specified adjustments; selecting appropriate scope and rates remains professional work.

assumptions: Shares are provisional for a manual-calculation workflow. OTHER is the building valuation application. This ends at the estimate, before any separate appraisal-report release or client send.

The appraiser verifies building/component ID, quantity, unit, selected rate, manual edition, location factor and price date in s1-s2. Measurement, source extraction and missing rates remain counted. Existing professional estimators produce their normal advice; no new estimator work is transferred free or credited to the appraiser.

Test native estimate tables first. Only 35 repeated manual calculation points are removed; existing calculator runtime earns no credit. s4 retains independent checks, exception repair, substantive estimate completion and ordinary save. Higher repair effort requires a lower benefit.
No new cost-review report or author-save approval is introduced.
unknowns: Actual calculation effort and native configuration
research_questions: Rebuild one replacement-cost estimate using the same scope and count omitted-rate corrections.

incremental.description: Maintain rate-edition mappings and unit tests

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Remove 35 arithmetic points less 1.5 upkeep. A heritage building requires bespoke estimator work and unsupported components; reuse only 7 points of standard quantity-rate calculations: 7 minus 1.5 = 5.5.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Draw land diagrams for appraisal reports

steps.what: Verify parcel sources, boundaries, dimensions and appraisal diagram requirements
Draw and adapt the actual parcel boundary and relevant land features
Place repeated scale, parcel labels and dimension fields in the land diagram
Check the complete land diagram and fit it into the actual appraisal report

tasks.design: Configure native diagram labels and scale fields in the geographic drawing application in {OTHER}. Retain boundary interpretation, actual geometry drawing and full report-placement checks in {DOCS}; remove only repeated label and field placement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Diagram production repeats labels and scale fields after the land geometry is drawn.
tasks.enabler_now: Native layout fields can reuse verified geometry and parcel attributes.
tasks.still_hard: Representing uncertain boundaries and relevant land features without misleading readers.
tasks.human_edge: Decide what the diagram establishes and what it leaves uncertain.
tasks.altitude: Less diagram annotation with unchanged appraisal responsibility.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: geographic drawing applications can populate scale and label fields from selected geometry and attributes; boundaries and diagram meaning require review.

assumptions: Provisional boundary is a real land diagram used in an appraisal report, not report submission. OTHER is the geographic drawing application.

The appraiser verifies parcel ID, source revision, coordinate system, units, dimensions, selected features and intended scale in s1-s2. Survey extraction, missing geometry and incompatible layers are manually handled there; no free newly digitised parcel source is assumed.

Native label fields are tested first. Only 20 repeated annotation points are removed, not fresh drawing or existing rendering runtime. s4 retains source checks, overlapping-label repair, report placement and ordinary save; larger repair needs lower savings.
No gate is placed on an ordinary report save. An actual external report send would be a separate action outside this diagram task.
unknowns: Existing annotation automation and layer compatibility
research_questions: Annotate a real parcel diagram using native fields and count scale and overlap corrections.

incremental.description: Maintain diagram styles and output-scale examples

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Remove 20 annotation points less 1 upkeep. A complex parcel needs bespoke labels and unresolved boundary notes; reuse only 4 points of verified scale and ordinary parcel fields: 4 minus 1 = 3.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review property changes from construction or demolition

steps.what: Read existing property records and verify construction or demolition source notices
Match explicit parcel identifiers and dates to flag changed property records
Inspect and review actual property changes within the jurisdiction
Determine which construction or demolition changes actually affect the property record
Update the existing assessment property record with verified changes

tasks.design: Test native parcel matching in the assessment application in {OTHER}. Use existing construction and demolition notices to flag explicit identifier changes, retaining source reading, actual property review, assessor conclusions and normal assessment-record updates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Regular reviews repeat parcel and notice comparisons before substantive property assessment.
tasks.enabler_now: Exact identifiers and dates can support a review list without deciding whether work occurred.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing notices from completed changes and recognizing unreported work.
tasks.human_edge: Determine the actual changed property characteristics from evidence and inspection.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated parcel matching with unchanged assessment authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: assessment applications can match explicit parcel identifiers and notice dates, but notices do not prove actual completed construction or demolition.

assumptions: Provisional workflow is an assessor's existing review and property-characteristic update. OTHER is the assessment property application; the record is used for assessment, not a new activity log. If the actual workflow is review-only, remove s5 and reweight without inventing a record.

Existing notice producers supply notice ID, parcel ID, notice type and date. The assessor verifies source and identity in s1; missing identifiers, address ambiguity and extraction are manually resolved there and in s4. No new free notice feed is assumed.

Native matching is assessed first. Only 20 repeated manual identifier/date comparison points are removed, not existing data-feed runtime. Inspection, unreported-work review and exception repair remain; excess unmatched cases lower savings.

s5 is substantive original record maintenance and an ordinary author save, fully retained and ungated. Formal roll adoption, assessment notices and external sends are not assumed in this review boundary.
unknowns: Existing notice-feed access and identifier quality
research_questions: Replay one jurisdiction review and count ambiguous matches, unreported work and record corrections.

incremental.description: Maintain parcel mappings and notice-date comparison tests

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Remove 20 matching points less 1.5 upkeep. Address-only legacy notices leave just 4 points with reliable parcel identifiers; retain all other matching and actual inspection: 4 minus 1.5 = 2.5.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain property, income and replacement-cost judgements while reducing specified arithmetic, diagram annotation and parcel comparisons.
